blocks.text: The reality of account executive roles and responsibilities

Your job description covers a lot of ground. You are expected to manage pipelines, nurture leads, and close deals. However, the reality of account executive roles and responsibilities often involves a heavy layer of administrative maintenance. Research shows that sales reps spend about 31% to 40% of their week on administrative work. This leaves little room for the high-value conversations that actually drive revenue.

The friction you feel is usually caused by disconnected software. You might have your CRM open in one browser tab, your email in another, and Slack running in the background. Moving data between these systems manually is error-prone. In fact, over 50% of professionals report that manual data entry leads to costly mistakes. When you have to copy information from an email and paste it into a CRM record, you lose momentum. This is compounded by the fact that many sales teams use five to eight different tools daily. Switching between these apps costs you 3 to 5 hours every single week.
Fixing your workflow without spending money

You do not need an expensive suite of tools to start improving your day. Start by conducting a simple time audit. Track what you do for three days. Identify the tasks that repeat every hour, like logging calls or sending standard follow-up emails. Once you know where your time goes, standardize your process. Create templates for your most common emails and use keyboard shortcuts to speed up your navigation. If you use macOS, learn the built-in features like Text Replacement in System Settings > Keyboard. This allows you to type a short trigger like 'sig1' to automatically insert your full professional signature.
Use the native macOS Spotlight search by pressing ⌘ + Space to launch apps instantly. Stop clicking through your Dock or Launchpad to find your CRM or email client.

blocks.text: How Lazur helps you stay in the zone

Lazur is built to reduce the friction of working on a Mac. It lives in your notch and waits for your command. When you are deep in a proposal or managing a complex thread in Slack, you do not want to hunt for a menu item or click through multiple windows. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur a question about your screen. It will answer out loud, allowing you to stay focused on your work. If you need to dictate a quick note after a call, hold the fn key to type clean, formatted text directly into your CRM or email app.
A daily routine for account executives

items: Morning: Review your calendar and open your primary CRM and email tabs in a dedicated Chrome window.
Mid-morning: Focus on high-value outreach. Dictate your follow-up notes using the fn key to save time.
Afternoon: Use ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur for help with navigation if you get stuck in a complex web interface.
Evening: Clear your inbox and update your pipeline status before signing off.

faq.question: How much time do account executives spend on admin tasks?
faq.answer: Research indicates that sales representatives spend approximately 31% to 40% of their workweek on administrative tasks, leaving less than 30% for direct selling.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files, or operate other apps for you. It provides guidance and answers questions out loud while you remain in control of your Mac.

faq.question: Is my data private when using Lazur?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur only listens and looks at your screen while you hold the shortcut. The audio and screenshots are sent to AI providers to answer your request and are never stored or used to train models.
